rationale: A is more decision-useful because it compares live alternatives more explicitly, includes fallback guidance, and handles uncertainty with assumptions and confidence intervals. Its quantitative support is helpful for discriminating among options, even if the estimates are somewhat unsupported. B gives clearer implementation detail for a hybrid model and practical operating rules, but it does less to test whether hybrid is actually better than the alternatives under different conditions. Since the task is choosing among structures, A better supports the decision itself; B is stronger on execution after the choice is made.
